text:
3.3.8. 跨职能敏捷
{
  "id": "G210:chapter-review:3.3.8",
  "source_section_id": "G210:s0026",
  "section_number": "3.3.8",
  "title_en": "3.3.8. Cross-Functional Agility",
  "title_zh": "3.3.8. 跨职能敏捷",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    28,
    29
  ],
  "translation_zh": "跨职能敏捷意味着每个冲刺团队都由业务开发、企业架构与敏捷解决方案开发能力组成，这些能力在同一团队内协作。不再有专门的业务开发、企业架构或敏捷开发团队，只有混合的、跨职能的自组织敏捷团队。所有改进工作通过业务变革与冲刺待办列表持续管理。\n\n这会带来额外的积极效果：\n\n- 汇聚有效交付客户价值所需的全部技能；\n- 为团队带来新洞察，以定义创造性解决方案并增强开发；\n- 打破刻板印象，通过多样性激发创新想法；\n- 形成共同的企业语言；\n- 解决优先级冲突问题，改善冲突解决；\n- 实现跨组织对齐。\n\n第一个冲刺（冲刺零）将定义初始业务变革需求，帮助在业务开发、企业架构与敏捷解决方案开发团队协作下排序未来冲刺内容（图 3-5）。\n\n每次演示时，每个团队演示当前解决方案增量、拟议的业务开发（MVBD）与下一冲刺的企业架构（MVA）。MVBD 与 MVA 的创建确保所有利益相关者理解将获得什么、并能影响结果。\n\n每次回顾时，所有团队评估上一冲刺过程绩效并做出必要调整。规划每个冲刺时，所有团队使用业务变革待办列表为下一冲刺选择最具价值（最重要）的需求。\n\n采用此协作模式，跨职能冲刺团队将在下一冲刺中恰好及时地产出业务开发、企业架构与解决方案。\n\n\n\n示例：若干跨职能团队各自具备一定企业架构能力，在每个冲刺中创建解决方案，并在冲刺末协调工作。\n\n校订注：原文第一项积极效果写作“Closes access to all the skills …”，与本节汇聚三类能力语境不顺。本译按“近距离获得/汇聚所需技能”理解，保留该疑点，不据此解释为关闭技能访问。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G210:p0028:c002",
      "pdf_page": 28,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "3.3.8. Cross-Functional Agility",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G210:p0028:b005"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        126.789,
        234.361,
        144.69
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G210:s0026"
    },
    {
      "id": "G210:p0028:c003",
      "pdf_page": 28,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Cross-functional agility means that each sprint team consists of business development, Enterprise Architecture, and Agile solution development competencies. These competencies are collaborating in the same team. There are no specific business development, Enterprise Architecture, or Agile development teams, just mixed cross-functional self-organizing Agile teams. All improvement work is constantly managed through the business change and sprint backlogs.",
      "source_block_ids": [

4.1. 阶段 A——演进式方法
{
  "id": "G210:chapter-review:4.1",
  "source_section_id": "G210:s0028",
  "section_number": "4.1",
  "title_en": "4.1. Phase A – Evolutionary Approach",
  "title_zh": "4.1. 阶段 A——演进式方法",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    30
  ],
  "translation_zh": "阶段 A 的主要目标是快速创建或确认拟议企业架构所交付成果、能力与业务价值的高层愿景。该愿景很可能随业务与技术环境变化及业务、开发团队反馈，在每个 MVA 中贯穿整个过程演进。但演进并不意味着这些变化必然是革命性的；因此拟议愿景应以允许演进与扩展的方式创建，并被视为企业架构构建的坚实基础，为在其范围与时间框架内工作的团队提供指导。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G210:p0030:c003",
      "pdf_page": 30,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "4.1. Phase A – Evolutionary Approach",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G210:p0030:b006"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        163.334,
        371.448,
        188.12
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G210:s0028"
    },
    {
      "id": "G210:p0030:c004",
      "pdf_page": 30,
      "content_index_zero_based": 4,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "The main objective of Phase A is to quickly create or confirm the high-level aspirational vision of the outcomes, capabilities, and business value to be delivered as a result of the proposed Enterprise Architecture. This vision will likely evolve throughout the whole process with each MVA based on the changing business and technology environment and feedback from the business and development teams. However, evolution does not mean that those changes will necessarily be revolutionary. That is why the proposed vision should be created in a way that allows evolution and extension. It should be treated as the firm foundation on which Enterprise Architecture is built, providing guidance to the teams working within its scope and time frame.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G210:p0030:b007",
        "G210:p0030:b008",
        "G210:p0030:b009",
        "G210:p0030:b010",
        "G210:p0030:b011",
        "G210:p0030:b012",
        "G210:p0030:b013",
        "G210:p0030:b014"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        197.87,
        563.76,
        322.61
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    }
  ],
  "semantic_rules": [
    {

4.3. 阶段 E 与 F
{
  "id": "G210:chapter-review:4.3",

  "section_number": "4.3",
  "title_en": "4.3. Phases E and F",

  "status": "source-compared-revised",

  "translation_zh": "阶段 E（路线图部分）与 F 需适配冲刺。并非所有步骤的所有部分都要在每个冲刺中执行；两个阶段各步骤的工作需适配每个冲刺的工作量。在解决方案团队众多的情况下，解决方案团队与解决方案接收方之间需要协调的工作更多。\n\n**阶段 E 步骤及可能的适配：**\n\n- **确定/确认关键企业变革属性**：确保理解接收方利益相关者的变革潜力。若同一批利益相关者接收整个产品，在首个冲刺（发布）中做一次可能就足够。\n- **确定实施的业务约束**：识别可能影响实施的新业务约束。每个冲刺都应做；也可在一组冲刺结束时做，以处理敏捷团队交付之间或与打包解决方案交付相关的潜在关联。\n- **评审并汇总阶段 B–D 的差距分析结果**：常规 SBB 工作（参见《TOGAF 标准——应用 ADM（架构分区）》）。\n- **评审相关业务职能的汇总需求**：管理解决方案的整套需求，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **汇总并协调互操作性需求**：确保冲刺范围内的互操作性得到汇总与协调；应在每个冲刺范围内执行。\n- **细化并验证依赖关系**：细化并验证冲刺中敏捷团队之间的依赖，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **确认业务转型的就绪度与风险**：确保组织/客户为 MVP 做好准备，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **制定实施与迁移策略（IMS）**：为冲刺制定足够详细的 IMS，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **识别并分组主要工作包**：识别所有敏捷团队（业务、架构、解决方案）在冲刺中需要做的工作，每个冲刺都应做，并作为待办列表输入。\n- **识别过渡架构**：确定冲刺结果应如何使用（迁移给所有用户还是仅特定用户群），每个冲刺都应做。\n- **创建架构路线图及实施与迁移计划**：与产品负责人及敏捷团队协作定义待办列表，每个冲刺都应做。\n\n**阶段 F 步骤及可能的适配：**\n\n- **确认实施与迁移计划的管理框架交互**：很可能应在组织踏上敏捷之旅前完成。\n- **为每个工作包赋予业务价值**：每个冲刺都应关联业务价值，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **估算资源需求、项目时间与可用性/交付载体**：在冲刺规划期间完成，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **通过成本/效益评估与风险验证排序迁移项目**：在冲刺规划中用于选择下一冲刺内容，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **确认架构路线图并更新架构定义文档（ADD）**：更新冲刺零创建的总体路线图，并更新 ADD 以反映架构当前状态，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **完成实施与迁移计划**：即下一冲刺的待办列表，每个冲刺都应做。\n- **完成架构开发周期并记录经验教训**：即回顾的文档化，每个冲刺都应做。",

  "translation_zh": "阶段 G 的目标——符合目标架构与架构愿景——在冲刺中与传统方法实现方式不同：其一，合规方式不那么正式；其二，短冲刺周期允许及早发现不合规解决方案。\n\n- **与开发管理层确认部署范围与优先级**：通常在冲刺开始时定义冲刺目标与范围时完成。\n- **识别部署资源与技能**：通常在每个冲刺开始、每次实施时完成。\n- **指导解决方案部署的开发**：通过实施指导开发团队的非正式过程。\n- **执行企业架构合规性审查**：与传统方法的区别在于审查方式——这是持续过程，而非特定时点的门禁/评审。\n- **实施业务与 IT 运营**：每个演示获批的冲刺之后，可部署一个解决方案增量。\n- **执行实施后评审并结束实施**：由于冲刺中的评审是持续过程而非最终用户测试式评审，此步骤可能是对实施各部分以往评审的正式总结。",

  "translation_zh": "阶段 H 的主要目标是确保所交付解决方案兑现承诺并处理拟议变更。建议把阶段 H 中适用于变更管理的部分分离为独立过程。\n\n- **建立价值实现过程**：定义确保冲刺期间产生的业务价值被接收的过程。\n- **部署监控工具**：部署测量业务价值的过程与相关工具。\n\n以下适用于变更管理的阶段 H 步骤被分离为独立过程（该过程与敏捷冲刺并行运行）：\n\n- **管理风险**：从演示与回顾中收集风险并制定缓解活动。\n- **为架构变更管理提供分析**：分析业务价值监控结果；评估收到的其他变更请求并移入业务变革待办列表。\n- **制定满足绩效目标的变更需求**：定义变更请求，以处理业务价值创造不佳与风险缓解问题。\n- **管理治理过程**：属于冲刺工作的一部分。业务团队治理企业架构团队，企业架构团队治理解决方案团队，反之亦然。\n- **启动实施变更的过程**：属于冲刺的正常规划工作。",

5.2. 不同架构层级上的企业架构与冲刺

  "title_en": "5.2. Enterprise Architecture and Sprints on Different Architecture Levels",
  "title_zh": "5.2. 不同架构层级上的企业架构与冲刺",

    35,
    36
  ],
  "translation_zh": "到目前为止，本文档描述的是在**能力架构**层面使用冲刺。按 TOGAF 标准，企业架构可在三个层级创建：企业（战略）、分段与能力；通常从更抽象到更详细、从广度到深度。\n\n你可以在企业或分段层级使用冲刺；上述第一阶段完全可照此使用。但进入企业与分段层架构时，情况会有所变化：这些层级的企业架构工作往往覆盖更大或更抽象的范围。\n\n在这些层级，业务开发与企业架构师之间的协作更有价值——此时看的是大局而非细节，但使用冲刺的方式完全相同。这会带来额外积极效果：\n\n- 业务与企业架构更早对齐；\n- 企业架构能够更早评估并影响业务战略决策；\n- 结果可用于业务变革待办列表的定义与排序。\n\n在这些更抽象层级需要什么样的解决方案开发？一个非常重要的结果是：可对需要解决的重要事项做小型（快速）**概念验证**（PoC），例如测试：\n\n- 拟议的流程变更；\n- 拟议的生态协作（使用简单沟通手段）；\n- 可能对业务模式产生重大影响的新技术；\n- 高级 COTS 产品（云或私有）；\n- 企业架构切片。\n\n每个 PoC 都应使用敏捷实践，由来自组织不同部分的小型、人才密集团队完成；PoC 是时间盒的，目标是测试与学习，但不交付可复用解决方案。结果反馈到业务开发与企业架构工作中，确保业务与架构决策得到验证。",

5.3. 冲刺长度

  "status": "source-compared-revised",

  "translation_zh": "冲刺长度取决于项目情境或性质，可为一至四周，但一般认为两周为宜；由项目管理团队决定冲刺长度。\n\n建议冲刺长度固定，使团队拥有可预测的可用时间，从而有助于短期与长期规划。若冲刺长度很少相同，团队将难以进行可靠规划。\n\n有人认为一个冲刺不足以创建足够的业务开发或企业架构，为业务或未来解决方案冲刺创造价值。确定项目适当“刺激—响应”时间时需考虑的关键因素包括：\n\n- 项目预期持续时间；\n- 客户/利益相关者：其提供反馈与指导的频率、公司或群体中的文化障碍、环境因素、团队经验、技术能力（自动化验收测试、测试驱动开发 TDD、自动化发布等）、工作分解能力——后者至关重要，因为冲刺应处理原子主题（理想情况下）或尽可能少的相互依赖。\n\n若无法在一个冲刺内完成足够工作，可让业务开发与企业架构工作跨越多个冲刺，但仍应把工作分成适合冲刺的块，且冲刺产出应对利益相关者有价值。\n\n另一种选择是定义一组过渡架构（发布）：当业务开发与企业架构达到一定成熟度后，敏捷解决方案开发团队使用发布材料，由业务开发与企业架构团队支持。这与敏捷发布列车（ART）密切相关；同时，业务开发与企业架构团队为下一发布准备材料。",

text:
5.4. 架构治理与冲刺
{
  "id": "G210:chapter-review:5.4",
  "source_section_id": "G210:s0037",
  "section_number": "5.4",
  "title_en": "5.4. Architecture Governance and Sprints",
  "title_zh": "5.4. 架构治理与冲刺",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    37,

  ],
  "translation_zh": "在敏捷世界中，需要以不同方式看待企业架构治理。\n\n治理是企业架构的重要组成部分，确保所交付内容符合基于企业架构层级期望成果（如长期愿景、目标与战略）的架构设计。\n\n业务需求、目标与战略仍是创造业务价值过程的重要部分，通常具有方向性且可能更长期；但企业架构的其他领域可通过基于冲刺中定义的优先企业架构决策创建解决方案来快速挑战、反驳或验证。企业架构治理过程被移入冲刺过程，企业架构与解决方案都可基于经验与学习被采纳和调整。治理由此成为一种协作、授权与相互治理的方式，通过对成果与交付的责任来实现。\n\n根据 Management 3.0 模型 [Delegation Poker & Board]，授权有七个层级：告知决定（tell）、解释并争取认同（sell）、咨询（consult）、达成一致（agree）、建议（advise）、询问（inquire）、授权（delegate）。该模型对称、双向有效：告知与授权相对，咨询与建议相反。这七个授权层级可用于定义敏捷团队（业务开发、企业架构、解决方案开发）之间如何分配决策权。\n\n治理的另一个视角是谁负责决策。Amazon 的 Jeff Bezos [Bezos, 2016] 提出两类决策：\n\n1. 可回滚的决策，授权给单个团队；\n2. 不可回滚的决策，需由包括所有敏捷团队在内的更大利益相关者群体做出。\n\nBezos 的区分有助于在建立企业架构能力与治理模型时取得恰当平衡；Management 3.0 模型则有助于考虑不同类型决策的不同授权层级。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G210:p0037:c010",
      "pdf_page": 37,
      "content_index_zero_based": 10,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "5.4. Architecture Governance and Sprints",

      "pdf_page": 37,
      "content_index_zero_based": 11,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "In an Agile world we need to look at Enterprise Architecture governance in a different way.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G210:p0037:b018"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        392.25,
        503.784,
        406.53
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G210:p0037:c012",
      "pdf_page": 37,
      "content_index_zero_based": 12,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Governance is a very important part of Enterprise Architecture to ensure that what is delivered is what was architected based on the desired outcomes for the level of Enterprise Architecture, such as long-term vision, goals, and strategies.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G210:p0037:b019",
        "G210:p0037:b020",
        "G210:p0037:b021"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        420.03,
        563.76,
        465.87
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G210:p0037:c013",
      "pdf_page": 37,
      "content_index_zero_based": 13,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "The business needs, goals, and strategies are still important parts in the process of creating business value, and are usually directional, and possibly longer-term, but other areas in the Enterprise Architecture can be quickly challenged, refuted, or proven by creating solutions based on prioritized Enterprise Architecture decisions defined in sprints. The Enterprise Architecture governance process is moved into the sprint process and both Enterprise Architecture and solutions can be adopted and adjusted based on experience and learning. Governance then becomes a way of collaborating, delegating, and governing each other through accountability for the outcomes and delivery.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G210:p0037:b022",
        "G210:p0037:b023",
        "G210:p0037:b024",
        "G210:p0037:b025",
        "G210:p0037:b026",
        "G210:p0037:b027",
        "G210:p0037:b028"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        479.37,
        563.76,
        588.33
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G210:p0037:c014",
      "pdf_page": 37,
      "content_index_zero_based": 14,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "According to the Management 3.0 model [Delegation Poker & Board], there are seven levels of delegation: tell, sell, consult, agree, advise, inquire, and delegate. This model is symmetrical and works in both directions. Tell is opposite to delegate, and consult is the reverse of advise. These seven levels of delegation can be used to define how decision-making is delegated between Agile teams (business development, Enterprise Architecture, and solution development).",

        "G210:p0037:b029",

      "pdf_page": 38,
      "content_index_zero_based": 0,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "One other perspective of governance is who is responsible for making decisions. Jeff Bezos of Amazon™ [Bezos, 2016] said that there are two types of decision-making:",

text:
关于 TOGAF 系列指南
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:series-guides",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0008",
  "section_number": null,
  "title_en": "About the TOGAF® Series Guides",
  "title_zh": "关于 TOGAF 系列指南",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "newly-translated-source-context",
  "pdf_pages": [
    6
  ],
  "translation_zh": "TOGAF® 系列指南说明如何使用 TOGAF 标准，以及如何裁剪以满足具体需要。\n\n系列指南预期是 TOGAF 标准中发展最快的部分，定位为标准的指导部分。TOGAF 基础内容预期保持长期稳定，而使用指导可针对行业、架构风格、用途与问题。例如，扩展企业转型所需的利益相关者、关注点、视图与支撑模型，可能与内部 IT 环境迁移到云所需内容显著不同；两者都使用 ADM，都从架构愿景开始，开发目标架构，并走向实施与迁移计划。TOGAF 基础内容是跨行业、领域和风格的必要支架。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G211:p0006:c006",
      "pdf_page": 6,
      "content_index_zero_based": 6,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "About the TOGAF® Series Guides",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0006:b014"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        277.254,
        332.31,
        302.04
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G211:s0008"
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0006:c007",
      "pdf_page": 6,
      "content_index_zero_based": 7,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "The TOGAF® Series Guides contain guidance on how to use the TOGAF Standard and how to adapt it to fulfill specific needs.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0006:b015",
        "G211:p0006:b016",
        "G211:p0006:b017"
      ],
      "bbox": [

        341.85
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0006:c008",
      "pdf_page": 6,
      "content_index_zero_based": 8,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "The TOGAF® Series Guides are expected to be the most rapidly developing part of the TOGAF Standard and are positioned as the guidance part of the standard. While the TOGAF Fundamental Content is expected to be long-lived and stable, guidance on the use of the TOGAF Standard can be industry, architectural style, purpose, and problem-specific. For example, the stakeholders, concerns, views, and supporting models required to support the transformation of an extended enterprise may be significantly different than those used to support the transition of an in-house IT environment to the cloud; both will use the Architecture Development Method (ADM), start with an Architecture Vision, and develop a Target Architecture on the way to an Implementation and Migration Plan. The TOGAF Fundamental Content remains the essential scaffolding across industry, domain, and style.",

1. 引言
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:1",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0014",
  "section_number": "1",
  "title_en": "1. Introduction",
  "title_zh": "1. 引言",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    11
  ],
  "translation_zh": "许多组织在管理业务复杂性方面举步维艰。它们希望回答关于战略目标实现进度的问题：战略投资是否投向了正确的地方？是否存在适合整合的冗余或重复？企业是否具备成功所需的条件，或者是否拥有过多？\n\n随着业务架构学科与实践的不断发展与成熟，“**业务能力**”概念已成为业务架构开发中的基础组件。业务能力地图是业务架构的四大核心要素之一，与价值流地图、信息地图、组织地图并列（参见《业务架构知识体系指南》[BIZBOK® 指南]）。\n\n业务能力以某种方式对业务现实进行抽象，帮助简化相关利益相关者之间的对话。定义业务能力的支撑组件（人员、流程、信息与有形资源），为这些支撑组件提供业务语境；为企业创建业务能力地图，则有助于形成对业务的共同理解。\n\n定义业务能力与能力地图是达成目的的手段。理解企业的能力，为架构师与规划者做出更好的业务决策奠定基础。这种洞察来自把业务能力映射到不同的业务视角；映射使更连贯的业务视图得以呈现。\n\n本文档试图回答关于业务能力是什么、以及如何用它增强业务分析与规划的一些重要问题：\n\n- “业务能力”究竟指什么？\n- 为什么业务能力是业务架构、企业架构及架构开发过程中不可或缺的部分？\n- 如何描述业务能力？\n- 如何（以及为什么）构建业务能力地图？\n- 业务能力如何映射到其他业务视角？",
  "source_units": [
    {

      "pdf_page": 11,

      "pdf_page": 11,
      "content_index_zero_based": 1,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Many organizations struggle with managing the complexity of their business. They want to answer questions about their progress toward realizing their strategic aims. Are their strategic investments targeted appropriately? Are there areas of redundancy or duplication that are suitable for rationalization? Does the business have what is necessary, or too much to succeed?",

      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "As the discipline and practice of Business Architecture continues to grow and mature, the concept of the “business capability” has emerged to become a fundamental component in the development of a Business Architecture. The business capability map represents one of the four core elements of Business Architecture, along with the value stream map, information map, and organization map; see A Guide to the Business Architecture Body of Knowledge® [BIZBOK® Guide].",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0011:b006",
        "G211:p0011:b007",
        "G211:p0011:b008",
        "G211:p0011:b009",
        "G211:p0011:b010",

      ],

    },
    {

      "pdf_page": 11,

      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Business capabilities provide an abstraction of the business reality in a way that helps to simplify conversations between interested stakeholders. Defining a business capability’s supporting components (people, processes, information, and tangible resources) provides a business context for those supporting components. In addition, creating a business capability map for the enterprise promotes more of a common understanding of the business.",
      "source_block_ids": [

Understanding a business’s capabilities provides architects and planners with a foundation for making better business decisions. text:
2. 什么是业务能力？
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:2",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0015",
  "section_number": "2",
  "title_en": "2. What is a Business Capability?",
  "title_zh": "2. 什么是业务能力？",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    12
  ],
  "translation_zh": "在 The Open Group 内，**能力**（capability）被定义为“做某事的能力”。业务能力表示企业做某事的能力。更正式的定义如下：\n\n根据 Ulrich Homann [Homann, 2006]：“**业务能力是企业为达成特定目的或成果而可能拥有或交换的某种特定能力或才能。**”\n\n关键在于：业务能力界定企业**做什么**，而不试图解释**如何做、为什么做、在哪里做**。\n\n作为业务架构实践的一部分，我们把“我们做什么”与“组织内谁来做”、“业务如何通过该活动实现价值”区分开来。业务能力可以是今天已经存在的，也可以是为支撑新方向或新战略而所需的。整合进业务能力地图后，业务能力代表企业可用于经营业务的全部能力。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c000",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 0,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "2. What is a Business Capability?",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0012:b001"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        34.086,
        397.908,
        64.38
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G211:s0015"
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c001",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 1,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Within The Open Group, a capability is defined as “an ability to do something”. A business capability represents the ability for a business to do something. A more formal definition is as follows:",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0012:b002",
        "G211:p0012:b003"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        73.73,
        563.76,
        103.79
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c002",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "According to Ulrich Homann [Homann, 2006]: “A business capability is a particular ability or capacity that a business may possess or exchange to achieve a specific purpose or outcome.”",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0012:b004",
        "G211:p0012:b005"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        117.29,
        563.76,
        147.35
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c003",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Critically, a business capability delineates what a business does without attempting to explain how, why, or where the business uses the capability.",

      "text_en": "As part of the practice of Business Architecture, we separate the concern of what we do from who does it within the organization and from how the business achieves value from that activity. text:
2.1.1 命名约定
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:2.1.1",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0017",
  "section_number": "2.1.1",
  "title_en": "2.1.1. Naming Convention",
  "title_zh": "2.1.1 命名约定",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    12
  ],
  "translation_zh": "命名为业务能力定义过程的第一步。它确立业务能力存在的清晰必要性，并有助于确保与其他业务能力清晰区分。\n\n命名约定采用“**名词—动词**”格式：每个成果（输入、输出或交付物）用名词描述，与产出、控制或监控该成果相关的活动用动词描述；例如“项目管理”（Project Management）或“战略规划”（Strategy Planning）。名词部分是**特定且可区分的业务对象**——业务所关注的单一、持久的事物。把业务对象作为业务能力焦点的好处是：它简化了识别与该能力绑定、并被其使用的信息对象的过程。\n\n业务对象通常是有形的（如“客户”或“贷款”），但也可以更概念化、无形（如“研究”）。最重要的考虑是使用能引起业务领导者和利益相关者共鸣的名称；通俗易懂的名称能增进理解、改善跨利益相关者群体的沟通。但要抵制直接照搬组织部门名称的冲动：与业务能力（本质上稳定）不同，组织结构并不持久，在多数组织中频繁变化。\n\n> 命名边界：原文把该格式称为 noun-verb，同时举 Project Management / Strategy Planning；这些英语表达采用名词化活动名称。中文“项目管理”“战略规划”按业务对象加管理/规划活动理解，不需机械套英语词性。“unique business object”强调焦点对象明确，不意味着某类对象在实际业务中只能有一个实例。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c007",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 7,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "2.1.1. Naming Convention",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0012:b018"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        410.369,
        206.645,
        428.27
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G211:s0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c008",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 8,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Naming the business capability is the first step in the capability definition process. It establishes a clear need for the existence of the business capability and helps to ensure it is clearly distinguishable from other business capabilities.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0012:b019",
        "G211:p0012:b020",
        "G211:p0012:b021"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        438.52,
        563.76,
        484.36
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c009",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 9,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "The naming convention involves expressing the business capability in a noun-verb format, whereby each outcome (input, output, or deliverable) is described as a noun and each activity that is associated with producing or controlling or monitoring the outcome is described as a verb; e.g., “Project Management” or “Strategy Planning”. The noun part of the business capability is a unique business object – a single, persistent thing that is of interest to the business. The advantage of making a business object the focal point of the business capability is that it simplifies the process of identifying the information objects that are tied to and used by the business capability.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0012:b022",
        "G211:p0012:b023",
        "G211:p0012:b024",
        "G211:p0012:b025",
        "G211:p0012:b026",
        "G211:p0012:b027",
        "G211:p0012:b028"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        497.86,
        563.76,
        606.82
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0012:c010",
      "pdf_page": 12,
      "content_index_zero_based": 10,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "A business object is typically tangible – for example, “Customer” or “Loan” – but it can also be more conceptual and intangible, such as “Research”. The most important consideration is to use names that resonate with business leaders and stakeholders. Commonly understood names enable better understanding and improve communication across different stakeholder groups. However, resist the urge to simply repeat the organizational department names. Unlike business capabilities (which are inherently stable), organizational structures are not enduring and frequently change in most organizations.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0012:b029",
        "G211:p0012:b030",
        "G211:p0012:b031",
        "G211:p0012:b032",
        "G211:p0012:b033",

      ],

  "title_en": "2.1.2. Description",
  "title_zh": "2.1.2 描述",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    13

  "translation_zh": "简短描述有助于澄清业务能力的范围与目的，并将其与其他业务能力区分开。一个有用的句式是把每项业务能力描述为“……的能力（或才能）”。例如，名为“战略规划”的业务能力可描述为“制定并维护组织战略计划与总体方向的能力”。\n\n与名称一样，所有描述都应使用与业务利益相关者相关且恰当的语言。两个重要考虑是：\n\n1. **简洁**：用一两句话提供恰到好处的细节，使理解超过仅凭名称所能获得的程度；\n2. **精确**：不要在描述中简单重复业务能力的名称，例如在描述“项目管理”时写“管理项目的能力”。",

      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "As with the business capability name, write all descriptions using language that is relevant and appropriate to the business stakeholders. Two important considerations are to:",

      "text_en": "1. Be concise: Provide just enough detail over one or two sentences to enable greater understanding than can be gained from the business capability name alone",

        "G211:p0013:b009",
        "G211:p0013:b010"

      "text_en": "A combination of roles, processes, information, and tools enables a business capability. The process of reviewing each of the business capability components helps refine the business capability name and description, and supports the subsequent analysis of business capability gaps, duplications, and redundancies. This decomposition can be used as a test to check that the capability definition is, in fact, a business capability (rather than a process, organizational function, or service).",

      "content_index_zero_based": 0,

The end-product of the modeling process is typically a business capability map, which provides the visual depiction (or blueprint) of all the business capabilities at an appropriate level of decomposition, logically grouped into different categories or perspectives to enable effective analysis and planning.",

text:
3.1 方法
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:3.1",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0025",
  "section_number": "3.1",
  "title_en": "3.1. Approach",
  "title_zh": "3.1 方法",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    15,
    16
  ],
  "translation_zh": "业务能力映射的第一个目标是捕获并记录所有业务能力，完整反映企业**今天所做**（不论做得多好）或**未来希望能够做**的全部范围。第二步是以合乎逻辑的方式组织这些信息（见 3.2 节）。\n\n识别初始能力集有两种方法：自上而下与自下而上。\n\n- **自上而下**：从企业层面识别 20 至 30 项最高层业务能力，每项均可分解为更细层级。高层业务领导者可协助初步开发顶层能力。实践中，自上而下起草能力地图更能有效利用时间，但通常只有高管实质性参与才能成功。\n- **自下而上**：时间更充裕时，可从业务各部分定义能力并自下而上构建。但若缺乏强有力的治理与高层领导支持，这种方法在跨业务协调上更困难，最终仍需形成企业级能力地图。\n\n通常，自上而下与自下而上相结合可细化能力地图。无论采用哪种方法，创建初稿都有三个良好信息来源：\n\n- 组织结构；\n- 业务模式；\n- 当前的战略、业务与财务计划。\n\n> 范围说明：20–30 项是本指南自上而下起步方式的规模建议，不是所有能力地图的硬性行数限制。选用何种方式仍取决于时间、高层参与和治理条件。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G211:p0015:c003",
      "pdf_page": 15,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "3.1. Approach",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0015:b012"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        258.014,
        166.734,
        282.8
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G211:s0025"
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0015:c004",
      "pdf_page": 15,
      "content_index_zero_based": 4,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "The first goal of business capability mapping is to capture and document all of the business capabilities that represent the full scope of what the business does today (irrespective of how well it does it) or what it desires to be able to do in the future. The second step is to organize that information in a logical manner. This activity is discussed further in Section 3.2.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0015:b013",
        "G211:p0015:b014",
        "G211:p0015:b015",
        "G211:p0015:b016"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        292.55,
        563.76,
        354.17
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0015:c005",
      "pdf_page": 15,
      "content_index_zero_based": 5,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "There are two approaches for identifying a starter set of business capabilities: top-down and bottom- up:",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0015:b017",
        "G211:p0015:b018"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        367.67,
        563.76,
        397.73
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0015:c006",
      "pdf_page": 15,
      "content_index_zero_based": 6,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "• Top-down: a top-down business capability mapping approach starts by identifying (from an enterprise-level perspective) the 20 to 30 highest-level business capabilities, each of which can decompose into more detailed levels",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0015:b019",
        "G211:p0015:b020",
        "G211:p0015:b021"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        56.881,
        411.23,
        536.504,
        457.07
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0015:c007",
      "pdf_page": 15,
      "content_index_zero_based": 7,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Senior business leaders can help to develop the top-level business capabilities in the first instance. In practice, developing a draft business capability map from the top down is a more efficient use of time, but is usually only successful if there is meaningful involvement from senior executives.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0015:b022",
        "G211:p0015:b023",
        "G211:p0015:b024"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        66.24,
        470.57,
        563.76,
        516.41
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0015:c008",
      "pdf_page": 15,
      "content_index_zero_based": 8,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "• Bottom-up: when more time is available, business capabilities can be defined from within different parts of the business and built from the bottom up",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0015:b025",
        "G211:p0015:b026"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        56.881,
        529.91,
        517.11,
        559.97
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0015:c009",
      "pdf_page": 15,
      "content_index_zero_based": 9,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "However, this approach can be more difficult to reconcile across the business without strong governance and senior leadership support toward ultimately developing an enterprise-wide business capability map.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0015:b027",
        "G211:p0015:b028",
        "G211:p0015:b029"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        66.24,
        573.47,

        619.31
      ],

    },
    {

      "pdf_page": 16,
      "content_index_zero_based": 0,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Usually, a combination of top-down and bottom-up approaches allows for the refinement of the business capability map. Regardless of the approach, there are three good sources of information with which to create an initial draft of the business capability map:",

  "translation_zh": "组织往往按与业务能力相近的方式构建：人员执行流程并分配资源或工具（资金、IT 或其他公司资产）。因此，组织结构可用于启发能力地图。\n\n常见错误是把组织架构图直接套用到业务能力地图的框架上。通常，多个业务单元会共同参与创造或交付同一项业务能力；组织结构本身也比业务能力更具临时性。应尽可能避免用表示业务单元的功能名称与顶层业务能力紧密对齐。\n\n例如，ABC 公司有四个主要职能领域，每个领域下有向父级业务单元汇报的较小部门，如图 3-1 所示。\n\n图 3-1：ABC 公司组织架构图。原图、图元与当前关系解释读取本节 structured_references。\n\n与组织架构图中各业务单元负责人初步调研后，得到如下初始能力集（名称已按上述命名准则调整）[1]：\n\n- **销售**：账户管理、客户管理、市场规划、渠道管理、合作伙伴管理、代理商管理\n- **财务**：财务管理、IT 管理\n- **人力资源**：人力资源管理\n- **运营**：资本管理、政策管理、产品管理、政府关系管理、分销管理、采购管理、运营管理、培训管理\n\n组织结构虽大致与能力对齐，但并不完美。组织中常见能力的重复或孤岛，因为组织并不清晰地对应业务对象。因此，需要分析初始能力集，识别业务对象并细化能力地图，使之更好地对齐业务对象。\n\n审视上述初始能力集，有些情况下“起作用的业务概念”并不清晰：\n\n- **IT 管理**：IT 通常是处理信息技术系统各方面的组织，因而常是重复的来源——IT 可能拥有自己的财务、人力资源等能力。若问与 IT 相关的新业务对象/概念是什么，最清晰的概念是“**信息**”。\n- **分销管理与采购管理**：分销与采购最好被视为价值流中的阶段。问题是：分销什么？采购什么？采购通常是采购资产；分销可以是资产或产品。产品管理已是既定能力，而**资产管理**则是新的。\n- **政府关系管理**：问题在于“关系”是模糊概念，涵盖多种概念。例如，可能是试图影响立法的游说活动，也可能是确保组织遵守监管要求的合规工作。因此，**监管合规管理**是潜在能力；通过游说影响法规可视为该能力的一个方面。\n- **业务规划**：有些能力与组织中的特定业务单元没有清晰对应，因而在基于组织结构的分析中可能被遗漏。战略业务规划可能由多个业务单元在不同层级开展，其中没有一个把业务规划作为唯一甚至主要职责。\n\n经过分析，得到如下一级能力候选清单：\n\n- **ABC 公司**：业务规划\n- **销售**：账户管理、客户管理、市场规划、渠道管理、合作伙伴管理、代理商管理\n- **财务**：财务管理、信息管理\n- **人力资源**：人力资源管理\n- **运营**：资本管理、政策管理、产品管理、监管合规管理、资产管理、运营管理、培训管理\n\n这一细化程度有助于识别跨组织单元的能力重复、冗余或缺口。\n\n> 示例边界：IT 管理细化为信息管理、分销/采购转向资产或产品管理、政府关系转向监管合规，是 ABC 示例的候选概念分析，不是禁止任何企业使用“采购管理”之类能力名。候选清单也不保证穷尽全部业务能力；原文尾注 [1] 明确首轮调查可能不完整。后续图 3-2/图 5-1 仍有旧名称，版本身份和图内文字应保留，不据同一位置自动合并。",

  "translation_zh": "业务能力是执行组织业务模式的构建块。若已有总体业务模式，可据此推导出支撑各核心业务模式要素的单项业务能力。把单项业务能力反向映射到业务模式，还能确保组织的活动与投资紧密对齐，或以支持企业总体愿景与战略为目标。",

text:
3.1.3 战略计划、业务计划与财务计划
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:3.1.3",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0028",
  "section_number": "3.1.3",
  "title_en": "3.1.3. Strategic Plans, Business Plans, and Financial Plans",
  "title_zh": "3.1.3 战略计划、业务计划与财务计划",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    19
  ],
  "translation_zh": "使用已发布的战略计划与运营业务计划，识别组织视为战略性或核心的任何业务能力。这些业务能力能够提供竞争优势，或属于企业所针对的特定行业与市场所独有的核心竞争力。\n\n对业务财务计划的评估还应突出企业运营所必需的其他业务能力，尤其是消耗大量财务资源的那些能力。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G211:p0019:c016",
      "pdf_page": 19,
      "content_index_zero_based": 16,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "3.1.3. Strategic Plans, Business Plans, and Financial Plans",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0019:b022"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        494.339,
        410.238,
        512.24
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G211:s0028"
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0019:c017",
      "pdf_page": 19,
      "content_index_zero_based": 17,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Use the published strategy and operational business plans to identify any business capabilities that are considered strategic or core to the organization. These represent business capabilities that provide a competitive advantage or that are core competencies, unique to the particular industry and market that the business is targeting.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0019:b023",
        "G211:p0019:b024",
        "G211:p0019:b025",
        "G211:p0019:b026"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        522.49,
        563.76,
        584.11
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0019:c018",
      "pdf_page": 19,
      "content_index_zero_based": 18,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "An assessment of the business’s financial plans should also highlight additional business capabilities that are essential for the business to operate, especially those that consume significant financial resources.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0019:b027",
        "G211:p0019:b028",
        "G211:p0019:b029"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        597.61,
        563.76,
        643.45
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    }
  ],
  "semantic_rules": [
    {
      "id": "G211:3.1.3:rule01",
      "kind": "planning-input",

3.2.2 分级
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:3.2.2",

  "title_en": "3.2.2. Leveling",

  "status": "source-compared-revised",

    21
  ],
  "translation_zh": "分级是把每项顶层（一级）业务能力分解为更低层级，以适合相关受众或利益相关者群体的详细程度进行沟通。有些能力在建模过程中会自然分解，另一些只有在能力映射到其他视角时才显现。\n\n例如，高管可能只关心能力地图的一级视图；架构师与规划者则期望更高的粒度。分解层数只受“传达目标受众所需信息、或使企业能就能力差距做出知情决策”的必要程度限制。实践中常见三到六级。\n\n图 3-3 展示人力资源管理能力的分解：人力资源管理为一级能力，下含七个二级能力，其中“人力资源绩效测定”又分解为三个三级能力。\n\n图 3-3：人力资源管理能力分解。原图、图元与当前关系解释读取本节 structured_references。\n\n**尾注**\n\n[1] 该清单并非可能能力的完整列表——如同任何首轮工作，时间不足以会见所有利益相关者群体，或信息不足以定义某项能力。\n\n> 分解边界：三到六级是实践常见范围，原文未规定必须至少三级或至多六级。停止细化的依据是受众沟通与能力差距决策需要；能力子项分解也不等同于能力的具体运营实例。",

  "translation_zh": "作为业务架构蓝图的基础部分，业务能力地图可在战略层面、企业范围或单个项目层面带来收益。对企业架构师而言，能力地图的用途仅受架构工作范围本身约束，且通常始于此前在广泛业务范围内的工作。\n\n部分影响与收益包括：\n\n- 提供关于企业“做什么”的共同词汇，且不依赖特定组织单元、业务流程或技术；\n- 使业务关系可以按“有多少领域关联到同一项业务活动能力”来理解；\n- 通过映射到相同业务能力，聚焦投资与成本节约；\n- 通过回溯到共同的能力视图，把项目相互关联；\n- 在提出可能不正确或不完整的解决方案之前，确保利益相关者就“要交付哪些能力”达成一致；\n- 确定哪些能力为价值流各阶段提供价值交付手段。\n\n关于把业务能力地图用于组合与项目管理的强有力用例，参见《TOGAF® 系列指南：业务能力规划》[G233]。该文档描述**基于能力的规划**，即在目标与目的、组织能力以及变革举措之间建立视线贯通的方法。Business Architecture Guild 进一步阐述了相关收益与原则[1]。\n\n**尾注**\n\n[1] 参见 www.businessarchitectureguild.org。",

  "translation_zh": "热力图可展示多种视角，包括成熟度、有效性、绩效，以及每项能力对业务的价值或成本贡献。不同属性决定能力地图上各能力的颜色。通常采用“红绿灯”隐喻，一眼看出需要关注的能力。例如，能力成熟度热力图中，达到期望成熟度为绿色；差一级为黄色；差两级及以上为红色；其他颜色可表示其他状态，例如紫色表示该能力今天不存在但未来需要。能力缺失意味着重大差距。\n\n图 5-1 展示从能力成熟度视角审视 ABC 公司业务能力的热力图。\n\n图 5-1：ABC 公司业务能力热力图。原图、图元与当前关系解释读取本节 structured_references。\n\n可见，市场规划、政府关系管理与人力资源管理需要立即关注；合作伙伴管理、客户管理与培训管理存在一些问题但优先级较低；代理商管理是企业希望发展的新能力。业务领导者可据此确保投资与项目举措按适当水平排序并获得资金，把紫色、红色或黄色能力提升到期望成熟度。\n\n根据业务希望采用的标准、视角或镜头，可从同一能力地图生成不同热力图。其他热力映射示例包括：\n\n- 战略贡献；\n- 绩效/有效性；\n- 收入贡献；\n- 成本贡献；\n- 覆盖度（每项能力被一个以上业务单元使用的程度）；\n- 关键性（Criticality）。\n\n> 图文语境：绿色/黄色/红色/紫色及相对成熟度差距是本节给出的热力图示例，不是所有图统一遵守的行业色标。图 5-1 和其正文仍用 Government Relations Management 等早期名称，而 3.1.1 的候选清单已细化为 Regulatory Compliance Management 等新名称；不要无说明把其当作同一名称版本。",

    26

  "translation_zh": "为厘清业务流程与业务能力的关系，先厘清业务流程与价值流的关系会有帮助。随着流程管理界更关注端到端流程，并使用超越任务、角色、决策与事件描述的更抽象表示来展示流程如何实施，其与价值流的相似性开始显现：价值流原则更适合在抽象的端到端层面建模高层业务流程。\n\n在本文档语境中，业务流程使能业务能力；业务能力是组织为交付价值流所刻画的价值（给所描述的利益相关者）而必须具备的能力。换言之，业务能力提供执行流程所需的能力。\n\n> 关系解释：本节先说“流程使能能力”，又说“能力提供执行流程所需的本领”，分别讨论运营实现与组织能做什么。两句作为有方向、有语境的关系保存；不把 enables 当作严格类型继承，不因此把能力与流程合并，也不从中推导循环的执行先后。",

As the process management community becomes more focused on end-to-end processes and using more abstract representations beyond task, role, decision, and event descriptions to show how to implement a process, their similarity to value streams starts to emerge. Value stream principles become more suitable for modeling high-level business processes at an abstract, end-to-end level.",

text:
6. 结合 TOGAF 标准使用业务能力地图
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:6",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0039",
  "section_number": "6",
  "title_en": "6. Using Business Capability Maps with the TOGAF Standard",
  "title_zh": "6. 结合 TOGAF 标准使用业务能力地图",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    27
  ],
  "translation_zh": "业务能力与业务能力映射都是 TOGAF 标准第 10 版 [C220] 的核心特征。它们在**预备阶段**早期引入，作为“定义并建立企业架构团队与组织”过程的一部分，并用于确定现有企业与业务能力。**业务能力管理**（确定交付业务价值需要哪些业务能力的过程）也被确定为与 TOGAF 标准协调的重点领域。\n\n在**阶段 A（架构愿景）**，架构师开始识别企业为落实战略优先级必须具备的业务能力。这些以业务能力地图记录的能力需求，随后用于创建基线架构与目标架构的高层视图。\n\n对业务能力差距的详细评估属于后续**阶段 B（业务架构）**，此时应用热力映射来识别并分析差距。建议的热力映射视角包括成熟度、有效性、绩效以及每项能力对业务的价值或成本。\n\n在 TOGAF 标准——架构开发方法（应用业务能力）中，业务能力被反向映射到企业架构项目范围内的组织单元、价值流、信息系统与战略计划。这种关系映射更深入地揭示各领域的对齐与优化。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G211:p0027:c000",
      "pdf_page": 27,
      "content_index_zero_based": 0,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "6. Using Business Capability Maps with the",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0027:b001"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        34.086,
        500.582,
        64.38
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0027:c001",
      "pdf_page": 27,
      "content_index_zero_based": 1,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "TOGAF Standard",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0027:b001"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        60.266,
        225.384,
        90.56
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0027:c002",
      "pdf_page": 27,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Business capabilities and business capability mapping are both core features of the TOGAF Standard, 10th Edition [C220]. We see them introduced early in the Preliminary Phase as part of the process to Define and Establish Enterprise Architecture Team and Organization (see the TOGAF Standard – Architecture Development Method) and determine existing enterprise and business capability. Business Capability Management (the process for determining what business capabilities are required to deliver business value) is also identified as a focus area for coordination with the TOGAF Standard.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0027:b002",
        "G211:p0027:b003",
        "G211:p0027:b004",
        "G211:p0027:b005",
        "G211:p0027:b006",
        "G211:p0027:b007",
        "G211:p0027:b008"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        99.91,
        563.76,
        193.09
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G211:p0027:c003",
      "pdf_page": 27,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "In Phase A (Architecture Vision), the architect starts to identify the required business capabilities that the enterprise must possess to act on its strategic priorities (see the TOGAF Standard – Architecture Development Method). These business capability requirements, documented using a Business Capability Map, are then used to create a high-level view of the Baseline and Target Architectures.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G211:p0027:b009",
        "G211:p0027:b010",
        "G211:p0027:b011",
        "G211:p0027:b012"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,

text:
7. 结论
{
  "id": "G211:chapter-review:7",
  "source_section_id": "G211:s0040",
  "section_number": "7",
  "title_en": "7. Conclusion",
  "title_zh": "7. 结论",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    28
  ],
  "translation_zh": "业务能力是开发与优化业务架构或企业架构的关键构建块。把业务能力与其底层组件关联，为人员、流程、信息与资源提供业务语境——这些要素组合起来，以产品和服务的形式向业务利益相关者交付价值。\n\n把业务能力组织成业务能力地图，为架构师与利益相关者提供独立于组织结构的稳定业务视图。模型描述企业现在做什么、或未来某时希望做什么；这种抽象也帮助业务领导者管理业务固有的整体复杂性。\n\n最后，把业务能力映射到不同业务视角，有助于业务领导者做出更好的决策。",

  "translation_zh": "The Open Group是一个全球性联盟，通过技术标准和开源倡议帮助实现业务目标，并在900多家多元成员中培育合作、包容和相互尊重的文化。成员涵盖多个行业的客户、系统与解决方案供应商、工具厂商、集成商、学术人员及咨询人员。\n\nThe Open Group的使命是推动实现无边界信息流（Boundaryless Information Flow™），实现方式包括：与客户合作，捕获、理解并满足当前及新兴需求，制定政策和共享最佳实践；与供应商、联盟及标准组织合作，形成共识、促进互操作性，并演进和集成规范及开源技术；提供全面服务，提升联盟运营效率；开发并运营业界领先的认证服务，鼓励采购认证产品。\n\n进一步信息见原文列示 www.opengroup.org。The Open Group出版广泛技术文档，多数着重标准与指南，也包括白皮书、技术研究、认证及测试文档和商业著作，目录见 www.opengroup.org/library。",

  "translation_zh": "本文档由The Open Group开发并批准。进一步资料及工具、指南和其他资源见原文列示 www.opengroup.org/architecture。\n\n本文档的组织方式如下：\n\n- **第 1 章**说明本文档所提供的采用指导的范围；\n- **第 2 章**介绍数字技术就绪度的概念：描述所针对的问题陈述、对当前已发表文献的概述、采用数字技术的动机与驱动因素，以及本文档的重点与目标；\n- **第 3 章**阐述就绪度评估对组织的影响与收益，并回答“组织为什么应当开展就绪度评估”这一关键问题；\n- **第 4 章**列出并描述影响数字技术采用的因素，以支持渐进式采用；这些因素分类如下：\n  - **基础因素**：组织为建立最低可接受就绪度所必须具备的因素；\n  - **影响因素**：通过提供支持条件来增强或放大基础因素有效性的因素；\n  - **持续因素**：使数字技术采用制度化、以获得长期持续收益的因素；\n- **第 5 章**阐述组织为形成结构化方式而应采取的各步骤，以规划、采用、评估并演进数字技术的采用；\n- **第 6 章**提供指导，说明组织在走查 TOGAF® 架构开发方法（ADM）时，应如何处理数字技术采用的各项因素。本章的意图是为数字技术采用搭好舞台，并把这一旅程融入企业架构过程；\n- **第 7 章**总结各章，并进一步为组织踏上各自的采用之旅创造条件，目标是最终提升采用的成熟度；\n- **附录 A**包含完整问卷及评分指引，作为可直接使用的工具，帮助组织快速启动各自的旅程。",

  "translation_zh": "TOGAF®系列指南说明如何使用TOGAF标准，以及如何裁剪它以满足特定需求。\n\n系列指南预计是TOGAF标准发展最快的部分，其定位是标准中的指导部分。TOGAF基础内容预期长期稳定，而使用指导可针对特定行业、架构风格、目的或问题。例如，扩展企业转型所需的利益相关者、关注点、视图及支撑模型，可能与内部IT环境迁移到云所需内容大不相同；两者都使用ADM，从架构愿景出发，发展目标架构并形成实施与迁移计划。TOGAF基础内容仍是跨行业、领域和风格的必要基础。",

      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "The TOGAF® Series Guides are expected to be the most rapidly developing part of the TOGAF Standard and are positioned as the guidance part of the standard. While the TOGAF Fundamental Content is expected to be long-lived and stable, guidance on the use of the TOGAF Standard can be industry, architectural style, purpose, and problem-specific. 关于作者
{
  "id": "G212:chapter-review:s0010",
  "source_section_id": "G212:s0010",

  "title_en": "About the Authors",
  "title_zh": "关于作者",

  "pdf_pages": [
    11,

    13
  ],
  "translation_zh": "（以下所属机构为文档批准时的信息。）\n\n**Bharat Thakarar，Tata Consultancy Services**\n\nBharat 是 Tata Consultancy Services Limited 的高级顾问，在多个行业拥有 22 年经验。作为企业架构师，他在战略咨询、企业转型与实施项目的成功交付方面拥有良好业绩。他曾在多个地区的中大型企业参与云采用与数字化转型的战略咨询项目。他还执行过高价值的数字工作空间转型、云迁移与云环境规划项目。目前，他专注于利用数字技术开展企业级云转型、就绪度评估、云足迹优化、应用合理化、性能分析与业务流程再造等工作。他还是认证的 PMP 与 SAFe Agilist。\n\n**Dr. Pallab Saha，The Open Group**\n\n作为 The Open Group 的首席架构师以及企业架构师协会（印度）（Association of Enterprise Architects (India)）主席，Saha 博士被 IBM Smart City Connect 认定为思想领袖，并获《福布斯》杂志（Forbes Magazine）专题报道。作为 MeitY-NeGD 企业架构高级首席专家、印度管理学院维沙卡帕特南分校（Indian Institute of Management, Visakhapatnam）数字架构客座教授，Saha 博士就政府整体架构举措的相关事务为多个部委和邦提供咨询。他是《印度企业架构（IndEA）框架》与《数字服务标准（DSS）》的重要撰稿作者，也是《敏捷 IndEA 框架》的合著者，在这些文件被确立为国家标准的过程中发挥了关键作用。他曾是参与制定印度国家数字健康蓝图（National Digital Health Blueprint，为印度政府卫生与家庭福利部）的高级别委员会成员。他的研究成果被国际电信联盟（ITU）用作可持续发展目标数字投资框架（SDG Digital Investment Framework）的主要参考，他还撰写了 ITU 关于数字化转型的专题报告。此前，作为 Wipro 政府与公共部门架构实践的负责人，他入选为精英级的杰出技术成员（Distinguished Member of Technical Staff，DMTS）。Saha 博士已出版五本企业架构著作，其成果已被翻译为阿拉伯语、汉语、韩语、俄语和波兰语。Saha 博士曾担任安得拉邦企业架构（Andhra Pradesh State Enterprise Architecture，ePragati）的首席架构师，使其获得国际声誉。他曾两次获得由联合国支持的微软研究资助，并与他人共同获得新加坡陆路交通管理局（Land Transport Authority of Singapore）创新基金。他的研究成果被联合国、ITU、世界卫生组织、美国国防部、开放技术基金会（Open Technology Foundation）、Info-Tech Research Group、嘉士伯（Carlsberg）等引用；他还为世界银行针对蒙古、越南和孟加拉国的 EA 指南做出了贡献。他曾担任新南威尔士大学（UNSW）研究学位考官、联合国大学（UN University）访问研究员、美国计算机协会（ACM）EA Tech Pack 的专家评审人，并作为受邀教师在卡内基梅隆大学（Carnegie Mellon University）授课。他在将企业架构引入 IIM 维沙卡帕特南分校与印度理工学院德里分校（IIT Delhi）研究生（MBA）课程方面发挥了重要作用。\n\n**Ganga Charan Gopisetty，SAP SE**\n\nGanga 目前是 SAP SE 子公司 SAP Labs India 银行与金融服务业务的首席架构师（创新业务解决方案）。他拥有 25 年以上国际经验，曾与 JP Morgan Chase、Barclays、Lehman Brothers NY 等银行以及 KPMG、PwC 等四大专业服务机构合作，涉足公司金融、资金管理、银行、风险管理、监管科技（regtech）与金融科技（fintech）领域——设计并实施框架与技术解决方案、提供风险咨询服务，并通过自动化再造业务流程。他是计算机科学工程师，拥有金融 MBA 学位。他的其他资金管理与风险资质包括 FRM、PRM、CTP、CISA，目前正在攻读关于新兴技术在金融服务中应用的博士学位。\n\n**Meheresh Masanpally，KPMG**\n\nMeheresh 是 IT 与业务转型专家，负责管理跨职能团队，在美国、印度和德国推动业务成果。他持有 TOGAF 9 认证，还拥有 ITIL、SAFe Agilist、ScrumMaster、Pega CSA、SAP PI 认证，以及巴塞尔治理研究所（Basel Institute on Governance）的“运营分析”与“财务分析”认证。他通过了 UGC-NET，并在金融、战略、市场营销与竞争法领域合著了多篇思想领导力文章。\n\n**Shailesh Agaskar，Capgemini**\n\nShailesh 是 Capgemini 云与数字实践（Cloud and Digital Practice）的高级企业解决方案架构师，在信息技术、业务、咨询与领导力方面拥有二十多年丰富多样的经验。他在大型复杂软件系统与软件产品的架构、解决方案构思、数字化转型评估以及端到端解决方案交付（以确保符合并达成业务成果）方面具备专长。他推动思想领导力、创新、架构治理委员会，评估新兴技术、技术与工具标准化及设计策略，促进工业化，并领导 Capgemini 内部的架构社区，同时担任有志架构师的导师。Shailesh 持有 TOGAF 9 认证，是 Capgemini IAF 实践者，并且是 The Open Group 与 IEEE 等行业论坛的成员。\n\n**Sripriya Venkatesan，Capgemini**\n\nSripriya 是 Capgemini 的高级架构师，负责重点客户的创新与解决方案工作。她持有 TOGAF 9 认证。她在 IT 行业拥有 18 年以上经验，曾为全球重要的《财富》20 强客户工作——其中一些是在客户现场，针对任务关键型复杂应用平台。她为不同行业的大型企业主导交付架构，并在服务型与产品型公司均有工作经历。她是其团队中来自印度的 AI 推广大使（AI champion），也是 Capgemini“Women in Delivery”计划的成员。她坚信，作为架构师，必须持续学习，才能跟上当今快节奏的技术发展。\n\n**Vishal Kumar，EY**\n\nVishal 是持有 TOGAF 9 认证的专业人士，也是本文档的工作组组长。他在政府与公共部门担任顾问，就职于 EY。他持有 ITIL 认证，并通过电信管理 MBA 拓展了职业经历。他在 EY 内部获得了设计思维与数字化铜级徽章（Design Thinking and Digital bronze badges）。他合著了三篇发表在知名期刊上的研究论文，主题分别为金融普惠、面部情绪检测技术与品牌传播。他热衷于参与社区活动，是 AEA 海得拉巴分会（AEA Hyderabad Chapter）的活跃成员。",

      "text_en": "As Chief Architect at The Open Group, and President of the Association of Enterprise Architects (India), Dr. Saha has been identified as a Thought Leader by IBM Smart City Connect, and featured by Forbes Magazine. A MeitY-NeGD Senior Lead Expert in Enterprise Architecture and a Visiting Professor of Digital Architecture at the Indian Institute of Management, Visakhapatnam, Dr. Saha advises various ministries and states on matters pertaining to government-wide architecture initiatives. He has been a key contributing author of the India Enterprise Architecture (IndEA) Framework and the Digital Service Standard (DSS), and the co-author of the Agile IndEA Framework, playing a critical role in these being notified as national standards. He has been a member of the high-level committee involved in the development of India’s National Digital Health Blueprint for the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. His work has been used as a primary reference for the SDG Digital Investment Framework by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), and he has authored ITU’s thematic report on Digital Transformation. Previously, as Head of Wipro’s Government and Public Sector Architecture Practice, he was selected as an elite Distinguished Member of Technical Staff (DMTS). Dr. Saha has published five books on Enterprise Architecture. His work has been translated into Arabic, Mandarin, Korean, Russian, and Polish. Dr. Saha was the Chief Architect to Andhra Pradesh State Enterprise Architecture (ePragati) taking it to international prominence. He is a two-time recipient of the Microsoft research grant supported by the UN, and a joint recipient of the Innovation Fund by the Land Transport Authority of Singapore. His work has been cited by the United Nations, ITU, World Health Organization, US Department of Defense, Open Technology Foundation, Info-Tech Research Group, Carlsberg and he has contributed to the World Bank EA Guidelines for Mongolia, Vietnam, and Bangladesh. He has been an examiner for research degrees to the UNSW, a visiting researcher to the UN University, an expert reviewer to the Association of Computing Machinery (ACM) EA Tech Pack, and an invited faculty at the Carnegie Mellon University. He was instrumental in introducing Enterprise Architecture into the post-graduate (MBA) curriculum in IIM Visakhapatnam and IIT Delhi.",

1.1. 概述
{
  "id": "G212:chapter-review:1.1",
  "source_section_id": "G212:s0014",

  "title_en": "1.1. Overview",

  "status": "source-compared-revised",

  ],
  "translation_zh": "数字转型正成为最新的行业挑战；多种趋势的汇聚，以及社会对数字技术工作、生活与连接（不受地理限制）的依赖，进一步放大了这一挑战。它正在改变互动方式与服务交付方式。企业不能再靠旧习惯与旧做法参与这场新的数字游戏，各行业都在被颠覆，且变化速度很快，再也回不到从前。已很明显：准备更充分的企业正在乘风破浪，而许多企业（包括新时代公司及其被过度炒作的商业模式）正在折戟。\n\n我们正在目睹五个深刻变化：\n\n1. 数字转型正成为全面、持续的必然要求；\n2. 颠覆者自身也在被颠覆，且颠覆速度加快；\n3. 企业正全面投入数字治理以驱动持续成功；\n4. 企业正在发现新的价值主张以求生存与繁荣；\n5. 驾驭数字技术正成为普遍的组织能力。\n\n数字技术的采用日益成为加速转型的关键成功因素。企业希望凭借“多聪明地驾驭数字技术实现业务成果”来区别于竞争对手。“数字 virtuosity（数字精湛度）”已成为组织肌理的关键部分。\n\n本文档涵盖任何组织采用数字技术的关键要义，其应用在设计上技术中立。读者将获得可用于采用数字技术的明确路线图。必须注意：本文档覆盖数字技术**采用**的路线图，即聚焦采用前（pre-adoption）方面，而非采用后的数字成熟度（post-adoption digital mastery）。文档意图是为读者提供一份可作为工具包的**就绪度评估**，评估以组织的整体视角构建。",

It is transforming the way interactions are occurring and services are being delivered. Enterprises can no longer rely on old habits and practices to play this new digital game, and this is causing disruption across all industries. Industries are changing at a rapid pace and will no longer be as they used to be. It is already apparent that better prepared organizations are riding the wave while many, including new-age companies and their over- hyped business models, are biting the dust. text:
1.3. 现有文献
{
  "id": "G212:chapter-review:1.3",
  "source_section_id": "G212:s0016",
  "section_number": "1.3",
  "title_en": "1.3. Current Literature",
  "title_zh": "1.3. 现有文献",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    18,
    19
  ],
  "translation_zh": "数字技术文献大多关注新兴技术的效能，较缺乏对企业如何采用这些技术、哪些因素影响采用、以及建立何种机制促成成功采用的研究。当前文献揭示了数字技术的趋势，以及这些趋势如何随各种动态而变化；也有研究考察了制约特定技术采用的挑战。既有研究多在“技术竖井”中考察采用因素（如组织因素对 AI 或 IoT 采用的影响），或研究技术扩散的驱动因素与宏观经济后果、采用滞后、沟通渠道与代理人的作用等。\n\n应用最广的模型包括技术接受模型（TAM）[Davis, 1989] 与技术接受与使用统一理论（UTAUT）[Venkatesh 等, 2003]，强调终端用户侧的采用因素；其他模型还有创新扩散理论（IDT/DoI）[Rogers, 1983]、FACC（功能性、可用性、复杂性、成本）[Dasgupta & Wendler, 2019] 等。这些模型把“技术”作为广义构造，未专门针对数字技术；另有若干专有采用模型。\n\n当前研究还显示企业架构师在敏捷创新团队中角色的演变：需要在数字格局中采取整体方法，要求多利益相关者方法与语境意识。在这一数字角色中，企业架构师充当决策促进者，推动新的数字产品与服务开发；人们看到企业架构师正在使客户旅程、流程与运营实现数字化。这些数字干预有助于优化价值链。在创建数字企业的这一新角色中，企业架构师在架构的所有层次上建立包容各方的透明度与端到端可见性（line-of-sight），从而便于找到正确的数字技术及其解决方案设计。\n\n现有研究还确认，全面的 IT 战略对数字技术至关重要。这促成了数字技术的成功实施，并有助于缩短概念验证（PoC）的周期。业界已开发出“创新互动框架”（Innovation Interaction Framework）等工具，用以描述采用新兴技术的运营流程、CIO 的个人领导力与组织业务需求之间的相互作用。这些框架有助于评估并对标组织就绪度。多项研究还提出了数字技术使能转型计划失败的原因，且大多倾向于给出应对这些原因的策略。显然，这些原因反复出现，以至于现在被称为“反模式”（anti-patterns），凸显其广泛存在。\n\n研究表明，新兴技术若存在明显的信任缺口，就会阻碍其采用。在理解数字技术方面存在“黑箱”问题。决策者与组织领导层必须理解数字技术采用可能意味着什么，以及最佳的采用方法，这一点至关重要。\n\n对现有文献的分析表明，需要一种技术中立的数字技术就绪度评估（DTRA）。已有大量研究在技术竖井中开展。在数字技术时代，随着数字技术栈不断演进，拥有技术中立的就绪度评估工具包已成必然。因此，以工具包形式提供就绪度评估，将有助于按已识别的关键因素评估数字技术。选择采用方法、执行就绪度评估、分析缺失因素的影响，并将这些因素与 TOGAF ADM [C220] 集成，这一过程对于形成全面的数字技术采用战略至关重要。这一需求与企业架构师不断发展中的角色相一致——在数字技术采用过程的早期引入正确的利益相关者。\n\n已有一些技术可用于评估组织进行业务转型的就绪度。理解业务转型就绪度评估相对于 DTRA 的价值主张至关重要：\n\n- 第一，DTRA 把专门面向数字技术的因素作为一个共同构造来捕获，但并不局限于任何特定技术本身；\n- 第二，DTRA 强调缺失因素的影响，帮助利益相关者根据缺失因素的主要后果来制定策略；\n- 第三，DTRA 包含企业成功采用数字技术所需遵循的步骤。\n\n本文档通过覆盖一个在当前全面推进转型计划的背景下日益相关的领域，弥补了现有文献所显示的空白。数字技术将继续存在、增长与演进。因此，本文档自然要尽可能让采用变得顺畅：帮助组织做好充分准备，并牢记——准备失败，就是为失败做准备（by failing to prepare, enterprises prepare to fail）。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G212:p0018:c001",
      "pdf_page": 18,
      "content_index_zero_based": 1,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "1.3. Current Literature",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0018:b011"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        209.034,
        236.286,
        233.82
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G212:s0016"
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0018:c002",
      "pdf_page": 18,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "In the main body of digital technology literature, there is a dearth of work on how enterprises adopt these technologies, what factors influence adoption, and what mechanisms are put in place to effectuate successful adoption. In general, the focus is more on the efficacy of emerging technologies. Current literature reveals trends in digital technology and how these trends change based on various dynamics. Also, there have been studies and research conducted on adoption factors about technology in silos; for instance, organization-related factors that lead to the adoption of particular technology like Artificial Intelligence (AI) or the Internet of Things (IoT), etc.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0018:b012",
        "G212:p0018:b013",
        "G212:p0018:b014",
        "G212:p0018:b015",
        "G212:p0018:b016",

      "bbox": [

    {

      "pdf_page": 18,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Studies have been conducted to understand the challenges that act as a constraint to the adoption of a particular technology. Additionally, researchers have identified various drivers of technology diffusion and the macroeconomic consequence of such diffusion. This includes analyzing the adoption lag across technologies. There has been extensive work done on the role of communication channels and other agents for technology adoption. Previous work has developed certain models having applications in various fields. The Technology Adoption Model (TAM) [Davis, 1989] and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) [Venkatesh et al., 2003] are most widely applied. These models underscore the factors from the end-user side of technology for its adoption. There are certain approaches and models defined in the literature. A few of the models researched are: Innovation Diffusion Theory (IDT) and Diffusion of Innovations (DoI) [Rogers, 1983], and Functionality, Availability, Complexity, Cost (FACC) [Dasgupta & Wendler, 2019]. All of these cover “technology” as a broad generic construct, rather than specifically addressing digital technologies. Furthermore, few other adoption models are proprietary in nature.",

text:
"text_en": "One thread of current work shows the evolving role of Enterprise Architects on Agile innovation teams. The need for Enterprise Architects to have a holistic approach in the digital landscape is brought forth. This requires a detailed multi-stakeholder approach and contextual awareness for the delivery of solution architecture. In the digital role, Enterprise Architects act as a facilitator for decision-making towards the development of new digital products and services. Enterprise Architects are seen to be enabling the digitization of customer journeys and the processes and operations. These digital interventions contribute to the optimization of value chains. In this new role to create digital enterprises, Enterprise Architects create all-inclusive transparency and line-of-sight across all the layers of architecture. This facilitates finding the right digital technology and its solution design.",

        "G212:p0018:b032",

    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0019:c000",
      "pdf_page": 19,
      "content_index_zero_based": 0,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Current studies confirm that a comprehensive IT strategy is paramount for digital technology. This has resulted in the successful implementation of digital technologies and has helped shorten the duration for the Proof of Concept (PoC). Tools like the Innovation Interaction Framework have been developed that describe the interplay between the operational process to adopt emerging technology, personal leadership of the CIO, and the organization’s business needs. These frameworks help to evaluate and benchmark organizational readiness. Multiple studies have also put forth the reasons for the failures of digital technology-enabled transformation initiatives, and most tend to suggest strategies to address these reasons. It is clear that these reasons are repeated so often they are now even being termed “ anti-patterns”, highlighting their wide degree of existence.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0019:b001",
        "G212:p0019:b002",
        "G212:p0019:b003",
        "G212:p0019:b004",

      "pdf_page": 19,
      "content_index_zero_based": 1,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Studies have shown that visible trust gaps for emerging technologies impede its adoption. There is a case of ‘black-box’ when it comes to the understanding of the digital technology. It is pivotal for decision-makers and leadership of organizations to understand what the adoption of digital technology could mean and the best approach for adoption.",

        "G212:p0019:b010",
        "G212:p0019:b011",

        "G212:p0019:b013"

    },
    {

      "pdf_page": 19,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Analysis of the current literature points to the need to have a technology-neutral Digital Technology Readiness Assessment (DTRA). There has been a great deal of technology-based research carried out in silos. In the digital technology era, the need for having a technology-neutral toolkit for readiness assessment is imperative with the ever-evolving digital technology stack. Thus, the requirement for a readiness assessment as a toolkit will benefit in assessing digital technology across the identified critical factors. The process of selecting the adoption approach, performing a readiness assessment, analyzing the implication of missing factors, and integrating the factors with the TOGAF ADM [C220] is critical for a comprehensive strategy for the adoption of digital technology. This need is consistent with the developing role of Enterprise Architects to bring in the right stakeholders early in the digital technology adoption process.",

text:
2.1. 概述
{
  "id": "G212:chapter-review:2.1",
  "source_section_id": "G212:s0018",
  "section_number": "2.1",
  "title_en": "2.1. Overview",
  "title_zh": "2.1. 概述",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    20
  ],
  "translation_zh": "已踏上数字转型之旅的大多数企业，正围绕利用最新技术以数字形式提供业务服务的关键方面开展工作。进行数字转型的企业最终必须采用数字技术，同时以信息技术（IT）为基础。根据《数字从业者知识体系标准》（DPBoK™ 标准）[C196]，**数字技术**定义为：“以产品或服务形式存在、可被数字化消费以创造或使能业务价值的信息技术。”\n\n传统上，企业使用 IT 使员工与业务能够借助硬件和软件运作。通常由 IT 部门负责运行一切（或管理与第三方交付部分或全部服务的合同）。\n\n企业在数字转型中也倾向于采用社交、移动、分析与云等各种战略。这些战略往往被孤立对待，无法实现端到端的数字技术采用。此外，用数字等价物替代物理资源并不等同于数字转型。DPBoK 标准将**数字企业**定义为：“以创造数字化产品与服务为特征的企业，这些产品与服务要么完全以数字方式交付（如数字媒体或在线银行），要么客户通过数字方式获得物理产品与服务。”\n\n更好地理解数字技术，还需注意以下几点：\n\n- 云、IoT、移动、社交媒体、分析、AI/机器学习（ML）等数字技术的性质不同；这些技术相互补充，而非与现有系统和信息竞争，从而以更少颠覆带来更大杠杆；\n- 数字技术及相关战略把数字与物理资源结合起来，使业务创新而非颠覆成为可能；\n- 数字技术被用来聚焦特定业务成果，而不是仅仅试图实施缺乏明确焦点、也无法看清所需努力规模的大型战略。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c002",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "2.1. Overview",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0020:b002"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        102.394,
        163.224,
        127.18
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G212:s0018"
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c003",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Most of the enterprises that have already onboarded the Digital Transformation journey are working on key aspects of leveraging the latest technologies to offer business services in a digital form. Enterprises undergoing Digital Transformation must eventually adopt digital technologies while keeping Information Technology (IT) as the foundation. As per the Digital Practitioner Body of Knowledge™ Standard, also known as the DPBoK™ Standard [C196], digital technology is defined as: “information technology in the form of a product or service that is digitally consumable to create or enable business value”.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0020:b003",
        "G212:p0020:b004",
        "G212:p0020:b005",
        "G212:p0020:b006",
        "G212:p0020:b007",
        "G212:p0020:b008",
        "G212:p0020:b009"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        136.93,
        563.76,
        245.89
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c004",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 4,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Traditionally, IT is used by an enterprise to enable the operations of employees and businesses to function in terms of hardware and software. Commonly, the IT department would run everything (or manage the contracts with third parties who delivered part or all of the service).",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0020:b010",
        "G212:p0020:b011",
        "G212:p0020:b012"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        259.39,
        563.76,
        305.23
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c005",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 5,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Enterprises, as part of their Digital Transformation, also tend to adopt various strategies like social, mobile, analytics, and cloud. All these are treated in isolation, which does not provide for end-to-end digital technology adoption. Again, substituting physical resources with digital equivalents does not equate to Digital Transformation. The DPBoK Standard defines digital enterprise as: “an enterprise characterized by the creation of digitalized products or services that are either delivered fully digitally (e.g., digital medial or online banking), or where physical products and services are obtained by the customer by digital means”.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0020:b013",
        "G212:p0020:b014",
        "G212:p0020:b015",
        "G212:p0020:b016",
        "G212:p0020:b017",
        "G212:p0020:b018",
        "G212:p0020:b019"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        318.73,
        563.76,
        427.69
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c006",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 6,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "A few things to better understand digital technology include:",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0020:b020"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        441.19,
        351.27,
        455.47
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c007",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 7,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "• The nature of digital technologies like cloud, IoT, mobile, social media, analytics, AI/Machine Learning (ML) is different; these technologies complement each other instead of competing with existing systems and information enabling more leverage with less disruption",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0020:b021",
        "G212:p0020:b022",
        "G212:p0020:b023"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        56.881,
        468.97,
        546.898,
        514.81
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c008",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 8,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "• Digital technologies and the strategies associated with them bring together digital and physical resources, enabling business innovation instead of disruption",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0020:b024",
        "G212:p0020:b025"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        56.881,
        522.31,
        538.425,
        552.37
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0020:c009",
      "pdf_page": 20,
      "content_index_zero_based": 9,
      "type": "text",

  "translation_zh": "每个决定开展企业级数字转型的企业，都需要评估自身对转型之旅的准备程度。就绪度评估衡量企业进行大规模转型的准备情况。企业不愿在不知道是否拥有资源来有效完成演进、并可持续地获得全部收益的情况下，启动大规模转型。\n\nDTRA 让决策者了解并确信：若决定推进，公司拟议的事业将会成功；同时避免因开展企业无准备完成的转型而导致高调失败，从而保护公司声誉。\n\n就绪度评估通常在高层次评估以下方面：\n\n- 转型目标与目的；\n- 期望、关注点与潜在价值；\n- 领导层对计划的支持；\n- 适应变革的能力；\n- 最小化潜在转型失败的方法；\n- 转型治理与决策；\n- 使转型发生的内部能力；\n- 其他关键计划需求，如流程管理与治理。",

text:
2.3. 当前格局
{

  "section_number": "2.3",
  "title_en": "2.3. Current Landscape",
  "title_zh": "2.3. 当前格局",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    21,
    22
  ],
  "translation_zh": "一项统计显示，高达 **70%** 的转型项目失败 [Bucy 等, 2016]；数字转型项目同样约有 **70%** 失败 [Morgan, 2019]。尽管多数企业与高管知道随技术演进、创建数字流程与解决方案至关重要，但付诸行动却是另一回事。许多企业启动数字转型后遭遇障碍便放弃。理解以下三个案例中出错的原因，可提供关键洞见与应避免事项的指南，为未来数字转型指明正确方向：\n\n- 一家全球跨国企业创建了新的数字业务单元，但注重规模而非质量；组织过大，无法一次完成整体转型，尤其缺乏对目标成果的真正业务愿景；\n- 一家大型汽车制造商启动了与公司其余部分分离的新数字服务，而不是整合数字解决方案；\n- 一家跨国消费品公司未考虑竞争或即将到来的经济危机；未审视行业动态——判断自己是否已领先竞争对手——也未关注经济状况。\n\n仅为转型而转型是无效的；转型必须考虑所有外部因素，并与战略紧密相连。\n\n这些失误可能给数字转型带来灾难，但三家公司都设法再次尝试，并取得了更大成功。",

Although most companies and executives know how crucial it is to evolve with technology and create digital processes and solutions, putting it into action is a different story. Understanding what went wrong with the following three examples provides critical insights and guidelines of things to avoid, to point future Digital Transformations in the right direction:",

      "content_index_zero_based": 15,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "• A major car manufacturer started a new digital service that was separate from the rest of the company instead of integrating digital solutions",

        "G212:p0021:b032"

      "pdf_page": 21,
      "content_index_zero_based": 16,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "• A multi-national consumer goods corporation failed to consider the competition or impending economic crash; it failed to look at what was going on in the industry – to see if it was already ahead of competitors – and what was going on with the economy",

text:
2.4. 动机与驱动
{
  "id": "G212:chapter-review:2.4",
  "source_section_id": "G212:s0021",
  "section_number": "2.4",
  "title_en": "2.4. Motivation and Drivers",
  "title_zh": "2.4. 动机与驱动",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    22,
    23
  ],
  "translation_zh": "因此，DTRA 成为必要之举：提前充分考虑所有关键因素，把风险与缓解策略、准备度以及变革意愿纳入转型路线图。这使就绪度评估成为启动或推进数字技术采用的前提。\n\n推动企业采用数字技术的一些因素包括：\n\n- **业务模式的演进**：数字技术使全新的上市方法与产品/服务组合成为可能。整条价值链受到影响，创造出新的客户价值主张与变现路径。技术驱动的业务模式变革正在扰乱全球经济的各个部门。成熟企业必须认识这些变化并转型组织，以缓解新威胁并利用数字技术创造的新机会。\n- **业务渠道的现代化与扩大客户触达的需要**：数字转型是把数字技术集成到业务的所有领域，从而根本改变业务运作方式及其向客户交付的价值。简言之，它改变企业与客户互动的方式，以及客户无论何时何地需要时都能获得一致体验的方式。事实上，当被问及影响数字转型战略实施决策的因素时，近半数组织将客户体验与客户满意度列为首要影响因素。\n- **云上不断增强的算力**：不断增强的算力与云的成熟，使大规模探索新的创新想法成为可能。这也使企业能够快速失败，并以迭代的、基于最小可行产品（MVP）的方法改进，或一次做对。\n- **互联网作为平台的普遍性**：互联网作为平台的普遍性使互联万物成为现实。这开辟了新途径，可探索收集的海量数据以形成洞见，驱动数字转型。\n- **开源软件的出现**：开源软件通过软件共创推动数字转型。基于社区、众包式的数字新技术开发与现有开源软件的成熟，通过客户与员工的参与创造积极颠覆，鼓励协作并提高生产力。开源软件便于快速原型化想法、试验流行技术，并在这些趋势上构建。\n- **技术创业者（technopreneurs）的出现**：技术创业者正在兴起，并通过数字技术创建成功的初创企业。他们提出想法，以挑战现状的不同思路带来颠覆；利用兴起的数字技术创建产品或解决方案，改变传统经营方式。这之所以可能，是因为数字技术的获取变得容易，而这又由不断增强的算力、廉价硬件、互联网作为平台的普遍性以及日益成熟和先进的宽带速度所驱动。\n- **数字企业作为市场颠覆者的崛起**：数字转型的核心，是利用技术、人员与流程对标准经营实践进行积极颠覆，从根本上改变业务绩效与成果。它关乎通过技术进步实现组织决策转型。组织可以更敏捷地工作，通过新思维与转变标准常规流程来扩展业务、增强竞争力。数字技术在帮助组织转变这些流程方面发挥不可或缺的作用，使组织能够推动更高水平的创新并轻松重构业务流程。对于希望启动组织数字转型的企业，重要的是聚焦“什么没有变化”，以加速采用并减少变革阻力。数字技术通过自动化流程帮助组织迈出下一步，让员工专注于高层次任务。",
  "source_units": [
    {
      "id": "G212:p0022:c002",
      "pdf_page": 22,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,
      "type": "heading",
      "text_en": "2.4. Motivation and Drivers",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0022:b005"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        126.354,
        276.678,
        151.14
      ],
      "source_section_id": "G212:s0021"
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0022:c003",
      "pdf_page": 22,
      "content_index_zero_based": 3,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Therefore, this makes the DTRA an imperative; the consideration of all the key factors well in advance to have the risk and mitigation strategies, preparedness, and appetite for change planned as part of the roadmap for transition. This makes a readiness assessment a prerequisite for onboarding or moving forward in digital technology adoption.",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0022:b006",
        "G212:p0022:b007",
        "G212:p0022:b008",
        "G212:p0022:b009"
      ],
      "bbox": [

        222.51
      ],

    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0022:c004",
      "pdf_page": 22,
      "content_index_zero_based": 4,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Some factors that are driving the adoption of digital technology adoption for enterprises are:",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0022:b010"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        48.24,
        236.01,
        510.881,
        250.29
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0022:c005",
      "pdf_page": 22,
      "content_index_zero_based": 5,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "• The evolution of business models",
      "source_block_ids": [
        "G212:p0022:b011"
      ],
      "bbox": [
        56.881,
        263.79,
        242.629,
        278.07
      ],
      "source_section_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "G212:p0022:c006",
      "pdf_page": 22,
      "content_index_zero_based": 6,
      "type": "text",
      "text_en": "Digital technologies enable radically new go-to-market approaches and product/service combinations. Entire value chains are impacted, creating new customer value propositions and monetization paths. Business model changes enabled by technology are causing disruption across all sectors of the global economy. Established businesses must recognize these changes and transform their organizations to mitigate new threats and take advantage of new opportunities created by digital technologies.",

text:
"text_en": "Digital Transformation is all about the positive disruption of standard practices of doing business using technology, people, and processes to radically change business performance and outcomes. It is about the transformation of organizational decision-making enabled through technological advancement. Organizations can work in a more Agile way and scale their business to become more competitive through new ways of thinking and transforming standard business-as-usual processes. Digital technologies play an integral role in helping organizations transform these processes. Digital technologies enable organizations to drive higher levels of innovation and to easily reengineer business processes. For organizations looking to kickstart organizational Digital Transformation, it is important to focus on what is not changing to help speed adoption and reduce the resistance to change.   "translation_zh": "开展 DTRA 的影响与收益是多方面的。DTRA 提供了一个机会，用于分析企业数字技术相关的现状。它围绕某些关键因素评估组织——组织哪些方面做得好、哪些方面需要改进，以及如何对转型/采用战略排定优先级。\n\n对企业架构师而言，这是一件赋能工具。以 DTRA 作为工具包，企业架构师可以利用其中的洞见来设计流程，克服数字技术采用的障碍。\n\n值得指出的是，随着企业架构师在新兴技术领域角色的演变，架构师如今被期望跨越边界、具备整体性。就此而言，DTRA 也有助于识别非架构领域的差距——通过突出已识别因素内部的差距，可以帮助业务理解其后果并弥补差距。DTRA 可以帮助识别数字技术采用的潜在障碍。DTRA 所带来的连贯视图，将促成高级管理层与领导层的及时认同。例如，对愿景或范围理解薄弱，或缺乏赞助，可能表明组织尚未对技术采用给予足够思考。\n\n开展 DTRA 的五项关键收益如图 3-1 所示。",

text:
4.1.1. 愿景
{
  "id": "G212:chapter-review:4.1.1",
  "source_section_id": "G212:s0026",
  "section_number": "4.1.1",
  "title_en": "4.1.1. Vision",
  "title_zh": "4.1.1. 愿景",
  "status": "source-compared-revised",
  "translation_mode": "revised-existing-translation",
  "pdf_pages": [
    27,
    28
  ],
  "translation_zh": "采用特定数字技术的愿景，是组织希望利用该特定数字技术实现增长、进步、提高可持续性或竞争力的愿望。一般而言，它表达组织为自身利益试验、采用或适应新技术的意愿或倾向，以服务于组织的总体愿景、使命或战略。它还给出期望成果与实现该成果所需的时间表。此类愿景的存在表明组织对技术采用的承诺及其行动的清晰度。\n\n在此验证愿景、动机以及组织对技术采用的承诺是否存在。\n\n愿景的清晰度有助于识别正确的发起人、为后续过程设定正确方向，并定义组织希望达成的范围与规模。因此，“愿景”影响“赞助与方向”和“范围与规模”因素。\n\n**案例背景（Case Context）**：一家大型银行在许多公司银行产品上处于领先地位，希望采用新技术以提供更好服务，并与规模更小、更懂技术的银行竞争。现有客户关系长期稳定，客户重视这种关系，但认为系统陈旧低效；临时性、按需的需求目前无法得到满足。随着客户自身技术规模扩大并希望银行配合，银行决定走“新技术”路线。\n\n思考：银行是否清楚自己想要达成什么？是否有关于目标位置的愿景？",

    {

      "pdf_page": 27,
      "content_index_zero_based": 2,

It also lays out the desired outcome and the timeline required to achieve it. The existence of such a vision shows the commitment of the organization to the technology adoption, and the clarity of its actions.",

  "translation_zh": "技术采用的愿景需要由组织高管与高级领导者明确、有力的赞助来支撑。识别发起人（个人或部门）可确立问责并提供权威。发起人定义使命与实现愿景的战略，确定高层路线图、关键利益相关者与开展举措/计划的预算。发起人的兴趣、在组织中推动愿景与目标的影响力、风险偏好（个人为追求目标准备接受的风险水平）以及组织对齐程度，决定执行的果断性与进取程度。对愿景的理解深度与实现愿景的热情，是采用路线图成功的关键。\n\n在此确认：发起人是否可用、发起人对数字技术的认知、战略与路线图的体现、风险偏好、发起人的影响力，以及其资金承诺。此外，发起人与支持团队（如自上而下的倡导者与变革管理者）的准备程度，在很大程度上决定后续行动及其成功。\n\n发起人的识别及其设定的方向，通过定义“实现什么、何时实现”影响举措的“范围与规模”因素；发起人预留的资金也影响范围与规模。\n\n**案例背景（Case Context）**：银行决定成立委员会进行现状审查并确定前进方向。由 CEO 与常务董事（MD）领导，CIO、COO、CFO 与 CRO 的代表组成。委员会首先被要求评估当前技术有多少可以保留、以何种方式保留，以及如何以较少的额外工作、投入与资金实现期望成果。CIO 提供所需的技术输入，COO 提供业务输入，供 CFO 批准业务案例并向 CEO/MD 建议预算。CFO 不了解当前技术，更不用说拟议的新技术。\n\n思考：银行是否有明确的发起人与单一所有者，能够做出决策并推动该举措？你建议采用何种赞助模式？",

text:
4.1.3. IT 能力
{
  "id": "G212:chapter-review:4.1.3",

  "translation_zh": "数字技术部署的所有权通常属于组织的 IT 部门。许多组织仍在与技术债务、根深蒂固的遗留应用和过时技术作斗争。采用数字技术有助于应对这一困境：一方面可借助新技术改善技术足迹，另一方面可创建更开放的信息生态以提升互操作性、改善用户体验，并吸引具备现代技能的新员工。IT 战略与技术路线图将驱动采用新数字技术的行动动机。当前 IT 基础设施、内部能力与应用全景是更好部署新技术的关键。架构委员会 [Davis, 1989] 的成熟度、采用 IT4IT™ 标准 [C24A] 以对齐和管理数字企业，以及聚焦的架构治理实践，有助于以有效、高效且持续的方式采用数字技术。\n\n在此验证：新技术采用战略、技术路线图、基础设施足迹、应用生态、架构治理成熟度与内部能力。IT 与业务期望达到的（目标）状态（即技术驱动的服务供给）以及 IT 在业务增长中的角色（使能者还是支持职能）也至关重要，因此需要验证。安全方面的总体政策，如购买还是自建、内部还是外包、信息所有权、升级与云采用，也是需要验证的重要方面。\n\n“IT 能力”受“技能与胜任力”和“生态系统”影响。内部技能与胜任力的可用性有助于快速开展 PoC 或试点并最终采用，也有助于组织定义新技术的支持模式；还涉及全行业生态、第三方供应商与产品供应商中可获得的此类技能与服务。“IT 能力”影响“实施方法”，取决于内部就绪度与成熟度。\n\n**案例背景（Case Context）**：银行的关键流程仍在使用遗留系统；虽然不时增加功能并进行升级，但在管理层决定利用新兴技术实施新 IT 战略之前，从未尝试偿还技术债务。\n\n思考：你对银行及其 CIO、CEO 有何建议？他们应先绘制结构化迁移到新技术的路线图（尽可能保留对遗留系统的投资），还是先为业务流程实施新兴技术、之后再考虑最佳映射方式？",

On one hand, it helps to embark on newer technologies to improve the technology footprint, it also helps to create a more open information ecosystem for better interoperability, improve the user experience, and attract a new workforce with modern skills. The IT strategy and technology roadmap will drive the motivation of actions in the adoption of new digital technology. The current IT infrastructure, in-house capabilities, and application landscape are key to the better deployment of newer technologies.
